name: Iamb-Tidal
geological_features: Polar ice shelves calving into temperate waters
specific_features: Alternating warm and cold current pulses with metronomic regularity
Marine fauna migrations synchronized to current rhythm
description: Iamb-Tidal is an oceanic world governed by rhythm. Its ocean circulation system produces alternating pulses of warm and cold current with a regularity that oceanographers find almost mechanical, a planetary heartbeat measured in the rise and fall of water temperature across predictable intervals. Polar ice shelves extend into temperate latitudes, their edges calving enormous bergs that drift equatorward before melting, distributing nutrients across the global ocean in the process.

The marine biosphere has synchronized itself entirely to the current rhythm. Migrations, spawning events, feeding cycles, and even predator-prey interactions follow the pulse with the precision of a metronome. The effect is hypnotic when observed from submarine vantage points: vast shoals of organisms moving as one, their behavior locked to an environmental clock that never varies by more than minutes across a cycle measured in days.

The mechanism behind the metronomic circulation remains poorly understood. Tidal forces from Iamb-Tidal's single large moon contribute, but models suggest additional factors are at work. Deep ocean surveys have discovered submarine mesa formations of unusual regularity that may channel currents in ways that reinforce the pulsing pattern, a geological infrastructure that acts as the planet's pacemaker. Whether this infrastructure is natural or engineered is a question no one has yet been able to answer definitively.

Fishing fleets have learned to work the rhythm, timing harvests to the pulse for maximum yield with minimum effort. The regularity makes Iamb-Tidal one of the most predictable and productive oceanic worlds in the sector, a reliable source of protein for nearby colonies. Conservationists warn that over-harvesting could disrupt the synchronized ecosystem in ways that would be catastrophic and potentially irreversible, but the steady drumbeat of demand continues to accelerate.
